title-group.article-title: Paired-biopsy analysis of TROP2 expression before and after sacituzumab govitecan in metastatic breast cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Westlake Comprehensive Cancer Center, Seattle, WA
Harborview Institute of Oncology, San Diego, CA
Midland Academic Medical Center, Columbus, OH

abstract.p: Background: Acquired resistance to sacituzumab govitecan in metastatic breast cancer may involve dynamic changes in therapeutic targets and associated signaling pathways. We evaluated longitudinal changes in TROP2 using paired tumor samples collected before treatment and at disease progression. Methods: Institutional databases were queried to identify patients with metastatic breast cancer who received sacituzumab govitecan and had paired pretreatment and post-progression biopsies. Samples were assessed by quantitative immunofluorescence and targeted proteomics. Marker abundance was compared within patients, and associations with clinical outcomes were explored using nonparametric tests. Results: Paired samples from 32 patients passed quality control. Median progression-free survival on therapy was 5.8 months. Baseline TROP2 expression was 2,140 normalized units, with a median on-treatment change of −24%. Substantial loss of TROP2 was observed in 12 patients, whereas the remaining samples showed stable or increased expression. Top1 changed by −18% across paired samples (p=0.08). The aggregate pattern was consistent with heterogeneous target modulation rather than uniform antigen loss. Conclusions: Longitudinal changes in TROP2 after sacituzumab govitecan were heterogeneous in metastatic breast cancer. Resistance was not explained by a single uniform biomarker shift, supporting multi-analyte assessment of paired samples and further mechanistic study. Research Sponsor: Translational Oncology Fund.
